Issue: Loan calculation RPCs can disclose another user's financial amounts
Evidence: loan_purchase_paid_amount and loan_purchase_due_amount are SECURITY DEFINER functions in the exposed public schema. They filter only by purchase UUID. No migration revokes their execution or checks auth.uid().
Impact: A caller with a known purchase UUID can request its paid or due amount outside the owner's RLS policy. Exploit requires a valid UUID. Hosted grants were not inspected.
Suggested fix: Add a migration that makes API-facing calculations SECURITY INVOKER with RLS, or moves privileged helpers into an unexposed private schema. Revoke EXECUTE explicitly from PUBLIC and anon, and grant only intended roles. Require ownership in any exposed definer wrapper.
Verification: Run SQL/API tests as anon and user B against user A's seeded purchase. Neither role should receive its financial values. Verify owner calls and allocation triggers still work.
Review method: Source inspection; default privilege behavior verified in official documentation

Issue: Late profile responses can restore a signed-out user's data
Evidence: fetchProfile guards pending-setting reconciliation by userIdRef, but unconditionally calls setProfile and writeCache after the request. The auth callback clears profile only for no session, and does not clear it when the user changes.
Impact: A response started as user A can arrive after sign-out or a switch to B, repopulating A's browser cache and displaying the wrong profile. Applying B's pending settings to A's result is also possible.
Suggested fix: Track an auth/request generation and check it before every state update, cache write and migration side effect. Clear profile immediately on user changes. Cancel or discard outstanding reads when signing out.
Verification: Delay A's profile response, sign out or switch to B, then release it. Assert no A data is displayed or recreated in browser storage.

Issue: Card payment tracking is neither atomic nor safe under concurrent payments
Evidence: The transfer, payment-history insert, statement read and absolute statement update are separate requests. createWithStatement launches tracking without awaiting it. Synced callbacks also launch tracking without awaiting completion.
Impact: Closing the app after the transfer can permanently miss statement tracking. Two payments can read the same statement_paid_amount and overwrite one another's increment. Queued payments to the same card can run their follow-ups concurrently.
Suggested fix: Move transfer creation, unique payment linkage and statement updates into one idempotent SECURITY INVOKER RPC or database trigger. Lock the card row and update the paid amount atomically. Use the same operation for manual, imported and recurring payments.
Verification: Save two payments concurrently and verify both are counted exactly once. Simulate a lost response and replay the same transaction ID. Verify rollback when an intermediate step fails.

Issue: Conflict detection can overwrite newer server edits
Evidence: A failed conflict read returns unknown and the write proceeds. The comparison uses the client enqueue timestamp rather than the revision originally read. The check and write are separate requests with no revision condition.
Impact: Remote changes made after a cached read but before enqueue are overwritten. Failed checks, clock skew and writes between SELECT and UPDATE/DELETE also allow lost updates.
Suggested fix: Capture the original server revision in each queued mutation. Apply a conditional update/delete against that revision in one server operation. Retain the item when verification fails and surface a retryable error. Reserve bypass for an explicit Keep mine choice.
Verification: Cover failed SELECT, stale cached revisions, skewed client clocks and a concurrent write between read and mutation. Each case must retain or flag the mutation instead of silently overwriting.
Review method: Reproduced with the existing fake Supabase client: failed conflict read and pre-enqueue remote edit

Issue: Imported offline transactions do not retain their optimistic IDs
Evidence: bulkCreateTransactions assigns UUIDs to optimistic rows, then queues the original values through enqueueInsert(values) without those UUIDs. The database generates different IDs on replay.
Impact: Edits and deletes before sync target nonexistent IDs. Lost responses or concurrent drains can insert duplicate financial transactions. Offline imported card payments also have no transaction ID for their payment-history linkage.
Suggested fix: Generate one ID per imported row and reuse it in the optimistic transaction, queued insert and all follow-up writes. Make replay idempotent by reconciling an existing ID and its owner/payload rather than treating every duplicate-key response as a new failure.
Verification: Import offline, edit and delete rows before syncing, and assert the same IDs reach the server. Replay after a simulated committed insert with a lost response and verify no duplicate or permanently failed item.

Issue: An edit made while a queued insert is saving can be lost
Evidence: The drain snapshots queued payloads. editQueuedInsert can modify the stored item while a request is in flight. mergeDrainResult removes a successfully sent ID without checking whether its stored payload changed.
Impact: The old payload is saved and the newer local edit is removed from the queue even though it was never sent.
Suggested fix: Version queued items and acknowledge only the version actually sent. Preserve a newer version as an update after the insert succeeds, or prevent editing the item while in flight with a clear UI state.
Verification: Pause an insert, change its amount in the queue, then complete the original request. Verify the newer amount is still queued and eventually reaches the database.
Review method: Reproduced with the existing fake Supabase client and editQueuedInsert

Issue: Pending receipts are handled only for queued inserts
Evidence: isPendingReceipt requires operation === insert. Offline edits can queue a pending-receipt marker in an update. An online upload failure can return the same marker while the transaction saves through the online path, with no receipt job queued.
Impact: The transaction can report success with an attachment that never uploads. resolveReceiptUrl explicitly cannot display pending markers.
Suggested fix: Represent attachment upload as a durable job independent of insert/update mode. Resolve pending files for both operations, and enqueue recovery when an online upload falls back to local storage. Do not store an unresolved marker as a completed server attachment.
Verification: Attach a receipt to an existing transaction offline and simulate an upload failure while online. Reconnect and verify the stored path resolves to the uploaded file.
Review method: Offline-update case reproduced with the existing fake Supabase client; online fallback traced in source

Issue: A connection failure after receipt upload can lose the attachment reference
Evidence: resolveReceipt removes the local blob immediately after upload and returns a changed payload only in memory. If the insert throws, the catch retains the original item with its pending marker. The next replay finds no blob and replaces receipt_url with null.
Impact: A successfully uploaded file becomes orphaned and the transaction loses its receipt after retry.
Suggested fix: Persist the resolved storage path before attempting the row mutation. Retain the local blob until that path is durably recorded. Preserve the resolved payload on thrown errors and add cleanup for abandoned uploads.
Verification: Upload successfully, throw before the row insert completes, reload and retry. Verify the receipt remains attached and no extra file is uploaded.
Review method: Reproduced with the existing fake Supabase client and a stateful receipt store

Issue: The shared queue has no cross-tab coordination
Evidence: enqueue performs a localStorage read-modify-write. singleFlight and listener sets exist only within one JavaScript module instance. There is no storage-event handler, Web Lock or transactional shared queue.
Impact: Two tabs can overwrite each other's enqueues or drain the same items concurrently. A duplicate insert may be reported as failed even when another tab already saved it.
Suggested fix: Use a transactional IndexedDB queue and coordinate drains across tabs with Web Locks or a persisted lease. Broadcast queue changes. Keep database writes idempotent because a browser lock alone cannot guarantee exactly-once delivery.
Verification: Enqueue and reconnect from two browser contexts at the same time. Verify all items remain visible, every mutation applies once and both tabs converge.

Issue: Optimistic changes are applied before the queue is durably written
Evidence: Offline creates update transaction state and cached account balances before enqueueInsert. Queue writes can throw on quota/storage errors, while cache writes silently skip those errors.
Impact: The UI can show a transaction and changed balance even when no recoverable sync item exists. Reload can then lose the apparent save.
Suggested fix: Persist the queued mutation before announcing or applying optimistic success. Return a structured storage error and roll back any optimistic state if persistence fails. Use IndexedDB and report unavailable durable storage.
Verification: Make localStorage.setItem throw a quota error. Assert the save reports failure, displayed balances remain correct and no phantom transaction appears.

Issue: Transaction requests can finish out of order after filters change
Evidence: fetch commits rows and loading/error state unconditionally after awaiting the request. Changing filters starts a new fetch without a request-generation check or cancellation. dedupeAsync shares equal keys but does not prevent results from older keys being committed.
Impact: Changing account/category/date filters quickly can display rows from the previous filter under the current controls, or clear the new request's loading state prematurely.
Suggested fix: Associate displayed data with its query key. Discard responses whose request generation/key is no longer current, and pass cancellation checks into readAllPages. Reuse a small tested request-state abstraction across affected hooks.
Verification: Delay filter A, complete filter B, then release A. Assert only B rows and B errors/loading state remain.

Issue: Reloading while online does not automatically drain pending transactions
Evidence: Automatic sync is attached to the window online event. The provider does not call syncNow when it mounts with navigator.onLine already true, and queue subscriptions only refresh counts.
Impact: Transactions saved offline can remain pending after the user closes the app and reopens it with a working connection. No online transition occurs to trigger replay.
Suggested fix: Drain on authenticated startup when online and pending items exist. Schedule a bounded retry for transient failures and check readiness on focus/visibility changes. Coordinate startup with registration of durable follow-ups.
Verification: Seed a pending item, start the app already online and verify it syncs without clicking Sync or toggling connectivity.

Issue: Mutation notifications do not refresh all affected data
Evidence: Account listeners only reload the cached accounts. useAccounts does not subscribe to post-drain sync notifications. Online transaction fetches do not refresh account caches. Transaction notifications reload each hook's own filter-specific cache rather than invalidating related keys.
Impact: Mounted account balances, Home totals or transaction lists can remain stale after online mutations, queue resolution or a mutation through another filtered hook. Cache events can simply reload the same outdated data.
Suggested fix: Introduce a shared entity/query store with explicit invalidation for transactions, accounts, budgets, goals and card payments. Invalidate or reconcile all affected keys after server writes and queue drain. Reuse one subscription contract instead of cache-only refresh events.
Verification: Keep Home/layout and a filtered list mounted. Create, edit, discard and sync transactions through another surface. Verify all lists, balances and dependent totals converge without navigation.

Issue: Opening a list offline without a cached result leaves loading active
Evidence: When no cache is found these hooks set loading true and immediately return on navigator.onLine === false without setting an offline error or clearing loading. The same pattern occurs in several cached data hooks.
Impact: A new filter or an expired/cleared cache produces an indefinite skeleton with no useful explanation or recovery state.
Suggested fix: Resolve offline-without-cache as an explicit unavailable state through resolveLoadState. Clear loading, name the missing offline data and retry when connectivity returns. Share this policy across list hooks.
Verification: Open an uncached account/filter while offline, and repeat with a cache older than its TTL. Assert an actionable offline state replaces loading.

Issue: Several history/export reads still stop at the API row cap
Evidence: Credit-card payment history, loan purchases and all-subcategory reads have no pagination. The configured PostgREST cap is 1000 rows. ExportDataCard uses these hooks as complete export sources.
Impact: Larger histories and exports omit records without an error. Missing loan purchases also omit their allocations and understate schedules.
Suggested fix: Use readAllPages with a deterministic total order for every potentially unbounded source, including these export reads. Batch large ID filters or replace them with joined server queries when URLs become too large.
Verification: Seed more than 1000 payment, purchase and subcategory rows. Verify reads and CSV exports include all IDs exactly once.

Issue: The account export omits archived accounts
Evidence: The shared useAccounts hook always filters is_active = true. SignedInExport reuses it for the full account export, although archived loans/accounts remain in the database and can retain transaction history.
Impact: A user exporting before deletion loses archived account records and the account context needed to interpret their retained transactions.
Suggested fix: Add an explicit includeArchived/export read mode or a dedicated complete account query, preserving the active-only behavior for normal account pickers. Keep the export dataset separate from display-only filtering.
Verification: Archive an account with retained history, export, and verify its row is present with Active = no and correct balances/metadata.

Issue: Cash-flow forecasts add native currency amounts to a converted balance
Evidence: buildCashFlowForecast sums occurrences * tx.amount without receiving a rate table or target currency. Its starting balance is stats.totalBalance, already converted. The card labels all forecast amounts using the base currency.
Impact: A USD recurring amount can be treated as the same number of PHP or EUR, producing incorrect projected income, expenses and closing balance.
Suggested fix: Move the forecast calculation to a pure src/lib helper and convert each occurrence into the base currency with amountInCurrency/sumConverted. Exclude and identify currencies lacking rates, including item totals and sort order.
Verification: Test a PHP balance with USD income and EUR expenses, same-currency rows and missing rates. Compare projected balances to independently converted amounts.

Issue: Savings-goal linked contributions ignore currency conversion
Evidence: totalContributed directly sums linked transaction amounts, subtracting expenses, without converting transaction.currency into goal.currency. The goal card formats that sum in the goal's currency.
Impact: Cross-currency linked transactions produce misleading contribution totals.
Suggested fix: Calculate contributions in the goal currency using the shared conversion helper. Keep missing-rate currencies visible and exclude them from the numeric total until a rate is available.
Verification: Link USD and PHP transactions to a PHP goal and verify the total at a known rate. Verify a missing rate is named rather than counted one-to-one.

Issue: Savings contributions overwrite concurrent increments
Evidence: addContribution calls updateGoal with current_amount = currentAmount + amount, where currentAmount comes from the rendered goal snapshot.
Impact: Two devices contributing to the same goal can read the same starting value and lose one contribution when their absolute updates overwrite each other.
Suggested fix: Add a SECURITY INVOKER RPC that locks the owned goal and increments current_amount in SQL. Give each contribution a unique operation ID for safe retries or record contributions as ledger rows.
Verification: Starting at 100, concurrently add 20 and 30 and assert the result is 150. Replay an operation after a lost response and assert it is counted once.

Issue: A failed savings contribution closes the dialog without showing the error
Evidence: handleContribution awaits addContribution but ignores the returned MutationResult, then unconditionally clears contributionGoal. The hook returns errors for offline and rejected writes.
Impact: The user can believe a contribution saved when it was rejected or never sent.
Suggested fix: Check error and errorDetail before closing the contribution dialog. Preserve the input and display a FormError or notification with a retry action, following the adjacent create/edit goal handlers.
Verification: Attempt a contribution offline and simulate a denied database write. Assert the dialog stays open and a clear error appears without changing the saved amount.

Issue: Some user-owned references have no ownership guard
Evidence: The transaction ownership trigger covers accounts, categories and subcategories but not the subsequently added goal_id. Transaction rules lack a category ownership check. Credit-card payment rows lack ownership checks for account_id and transaction_id. Their RLS checks only the row's user_id.
Impact: A caller knowing another user's UUID can create cross-owner relationships. Foreign-key checks bypass RLS, so RLS on the referenced table does not enforce this invariant. This is not evidence of unrestricted reads of those rows.
Suggested fix: Add composite owner-scoped foreign keys or ownership triggers for every user-owned reference. Validate a payment's transaction, destination and amount relationship as well as its owner. Backfill or repair invalid links before validating constraints.
Verification: As user B, attempt to reference A's goal, rule category, account and transfer. Each write must fail. Owner-consistent writes must succeed.
Review method: Source inspection; foreign-key/RLS behavior verified in official documentation

Issue: Bulk category changes can leave a subcategory attached to the wrong parent
Evidence: bulkUpdateCategory changes category_id only. The ownership trigger checks that subcategory_id belongs to the same user but does not require subcategories.category_id = transactions.category_id.
Impact: A transaction moved from Food to Travel can retain a Food subcategory, giving inconsistent filters, exports and category reports.
Suggested fix: Clear subcategory_id when changing the parent category unless an explicit mapping preserves it. Add a database guard requiring the selected subcategory to belong to the selected category, including subcategory reparenting paths.
Verification: Bulk-change a categorized transaction with a subcategory and assert the child is cleared or remapped. Attempt a mismatched parent/child insert directly and verify it is rejected.

Issue: An account currency can be changed without migrating its history
Evidence: The edit form exposes the currency selector and updateAccountWithAdjustment writes changed metadata. There is no server guard or history conversion when an account currency changes. Existing transaction amounts/currencies and stored balance are retained.
Impact: Changing a populated USD account to PHP relabels its balance while old transaction deltas still use the old units. Subsequent edits/deletes mix units in the same balance.
Suggested fix: Prevent currency changes once transaction or financed-purchase history exists, in both the form and the database. If currency migration is a required feature, implement an explicit atomic conversion workflow with a recorded rate and audit trail.
Verification: Create an account with history, attempt a currency edit through the UI and API, then edit/delete an old transaction. Verify balances never mix currency units.

Issue: All routes and heavy features load in the main JavaScript bundle
Evidence: App imports all pages eagerly. The production build reports a 2935.60 kB main JavaScript chunk, 844.40 kB gzip, and warns that chunks exceed 500 kB. The PWA precaches 3525.23 KiB.
Impact: Visitors must download and parse report/chart/import features before using login or basic account views. The initial app shell is expensive on slower mobile devices.
Suggested fix: Lazy-load route pages with React.lazy and useful Suspense boundaries. Load PDF generation, charts and import editors when needed. Adjust service-worker precaching deliberately so deferred features do not all transfer during installation. Measure before choosing extra chunk rules.
Verification: Compare production bundle sizes and cold login/Home loads before and after splitting on a throttled mobile profile. Verify offline navigation for installed features and update behavior.

Issue: Offline bulk imports repeatedly serialize the entire growing queue
Evidence: Each imported row independently reads/parses the queue, appends one item and writes/stringifies it. Each row also rewrites the account cache and emits notifications. Queue serialization grows approximately quadratically with imported row count.
Impact: Large permitted CSV imports can block the main thread, flood subscribers and hit storage limits partway through a save.
Suggested fix: Add a reusable enqueueMany operation that persists all rows in one transaction. Apply account deltas in one pass, update caches once and emit one notification. Use IndexedDB for larger durable batches.
Verification: Benchmark a representative 10000-row offline import and count queue writes and notifications. Require one durable batch commit and one coherent optimistic update. Verify all-or-nothing behavior on persistence failure.

Issue: CI validates migration syntax but not tenant isolation or financial concurrency
Evidence: The db job starts Supabase, lints functions and resets migrations. It does not execute a database behavior suite. Existing loan SQL tests use source matching, while queue tests use a fake client that does not model concurrent database transactions or RLS.
Impact: Passing 1126 tests does not detect the exposed definer calculations, lost concurrent payment increments or cross-owner reference writes described in this review.
Suggested fix: Add a focused database integration suite after migration application, using separate JWT/SQL roles and transaction connections. Cover anon and cross-user access, balance invariants, payment idempotency and concurrent writes. Add hook lifecycle tests for delayed reads and auth changes.
Verification: Demonstrate that the new tests fail against the current defects and pass after their fixes, including a fresh database replay.
Review method: CI and test-source inspection; existing test suite passed

Issue: The Supabase client lacks generated database types
Evidence: createClient is called without a generated Database generic. Database row shapes are manually declared and selected data is repeatedly cast to application types. DrainClient.from is explicitly any.
Impact: Misspelled columns, RPC signatures and schema drift are easier to ship because TypeScript cannot validate the API contract.
Suggested fix: Generate database types from the migration-applied local schema and use createClient<Database>. Derive entity DTOs and RPC arguments from them. Keep the fake client boundary small and typed rather than expanding any into application logic.
Verification: Add a type-generation drift check and confirm incorrect column names and RPC arguments fail the build while the pure helper tests remain runnable.

Issue: Common entity hooks repeat reads and loading/cache policies
Evidence: Each useAccounts instance fetches independently. Layout, payment handling and pages instantiate it together. Similar fetch/cache/offline/error logic is repeated across entity hooks. Only transaction reads currently use dedupeAsync.
Impact: The same account query can run several times on mount, and lifecycle fixes must be repeated in many hooks, increasing the chance of inconsistent behavior.
Suggested fix: Share entity reads through a user-scoped query store or reusable read hook with request deduplication, key-aware state and consistent offline/error policy. Keep entity-specific business mutations outside the shared read abstraction.
Verification: Mount layout, page and payment hooks together and assert one read per entity/query key. Verify request races, errors and offline behavior through the shared abstraction.
